vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: juejin-publisher
Version: 1.0.0

The skill automates article publishing to Juejin via its official API (api.juejin.cn). While the code logic in scripts/publish.py is functional and aligned with its stated purpose, the bundle includes a juejin.env file containing a hardcoded, realistic session cookie (JUEJIN_COOKIE). This represents a significant credential leak and security risk, although no evidence of intentional exfiltration to third-party domains was found.

llm.summary: The skill appears to do what it claims (publish Markdown to Juejin) but includes a hard-coded Juejin Cookie in the repository and fails to declare required credentials, which is a security/privacy risk and an incoherence.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the included scripts: the Python scripts call juejin.cn APIs to create drafts and publish articles. Required binaries (python3, curl) are reasonable. However the skill metadata lists no required credentials while both SKILL.md and scripts expect a JUEJIN_COOKIE configuration file (juejin.env) — a mild mismatch between declared requirements and actual needs.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions explicitly tell the agent to read a local config file (juejin.env) for the Cookie and then post content to api.juejin.cn. That behavior is consistent with the purpose, but reading a local file containing authentication material is sensitive and the repository actually contains a pre-populated juejin.env with a long cookie value — the instructions will cause the skill to use that credential unless the user replaces it.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec or external downloads — scripts are included in the package and run locally. No network-based installer or arbitrary archive extraction observed. This limits supply-chain risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requires an authentication cookie for Juejin, which is proportionate to publishing, but the package includes a committed juejin.env file containing a long Cookie string (sensitive credential). The skill metadata does not declare this required credential as an environment variable, and the presence of a prefilled cookie means the repository may operate under a third-party account by default — this is a privacy/credential risk and incoherent with 'no required env vars'.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and user-invocable default. The skill does not request system-wide persistence or modify other skills/configs. It only reads a local config file in its own directory.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill will read a local juejin.env file and use its JUEJIN_COOKIE to publish articles to juejin.cn. The repository currently includes a pre-filled juejin.env containing a long Cookie-like value — do NOT use that file as-is. Before installing or running: 1) inspect and remove any included juejin.env (or overwrite it) so you never use someone else's credential; 2) replace it with your own cookie obtained securely, or modify the script to read credentials from an environment variable instead; 3) review the two Python scripts to confirm they only call api.juejin.cn (they do) and don't exfiltrate data elsewhere; 4) if you plan to allow autonomous agent invocation, consider disabling autonomous calls until you trust the credential handling; and 5) if unsure, run the publish script manually in a controlled environment first to verify behavior. The biggest red flag is the committed credential in the repo — treat it as compromised and don't reuse it.
